title: Two-level receipt preference override rule stated twice
description: The rule that Chat.receiptSharing overrides PresenceStatus.receiptSharing at the per-chat level is expressed as normative text in two separate locations: (1) the Chat.receiptSharing field definition (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00.md ~lines 441-442): 'When present, this value takes precedence over the account-level setting for this Chat only. When absent, the account-level preference applies.' (2) the Peer/receipt Sender Behavior section (draft-atwood-jmap-chat-federation-00.md ~lines 305-306): 'if Chat.receiptSharing is present for the relevant Chat, that value is used; otherwise the account-level PresenceStatus.receiptSharing applies.' Both are normative and say the same thing with different wording, creating a maintenance risk if the precedence rule ever changes. Suggested improvement: make one location normative and the other a cross-reference. The field definition is the natural home for the rule; the Sender Behavior section should reference it rather than re-state it, e.g. 'the server MUST determine the effective receipt-sharing preference per the two-level override rule defined in {{JMAP-CHAT}} (Chat.receiptSharing overrides PresenceStatus.receiptSharing when present).'
close_reason: Resolved: Chat.receiptSharing field is canonical; Sender Behavior cross-references same logic without identical language
